wu: Job charades: Teacher acts out 3 jobs (doctor, teacher, chef), students guess and shout 'You're a [job]!'
wuAlt: Job Pictionary: Students draw jobs on the board for others to guess
Job Bingo: Teacher calls out jobs, students cross them off their bingo sheet
pres: Show flashcards of 5 jobs, model sentences: 'A doctor has to help people.' 'A teacher has to work in a school.' Ask students to repeat, then ask 'What does a chef have to do?' to check understanding.
presAlt: Job stories: Tell a short story about a day in the life of a firefighter using 'have to'
Job charades with prompts: Teacher mimes jobs and students say the sentence
prac: Job charades pairs: Student A mimes a job, Student B says 'You have to...' or 'You don't have to...' Teacher circulates to correct sentences.
pracAlt: Job dominoes: Match job cards to 'have to' sentences
Job matching worksheet: Draw lines from jobs to their duties using 'have to'
ls: Listen to 3 job descriptions (teacher, chef, doctor) and write the job next to each description. Check answers as a class.
re: Job relay: Teams race to write 'have to' sentences on the board for different jobs. First team to write 3 correct sentences wins.
prod: Dream job pairs: Student A asks 'What's your dream job?', Student B answers 'My dream job is a [job]. I have to...' Then they swap roles.
rw: Read a short job profile for 'video game tester' and complete a fact file with 'have to' sentences. Then write 2 sentences about their own dream job.
st: Sing 'What Do You Want to Be?' with gestures. End with: 'Today we learned to talk about jobs using have to. Great job, everyone! Thank you, class.'
g: Students take turns miming jobs while others guess using 'You have to...'
Match job cards to their 'have to' duties
Listen to 'have to' sentences and cross off the matching job
Ask 3 classmates about their dream jobs and write down their answers
Draw jobs on the board for others to guess the sentence
diff: Fast finishers / stronger learners: Write 3 more 'have to' sentences for their dream job
Support / weaker learners: Use a sentence frame: 'My dream job is a ___. I have to ___.'
hw: Complete the 'My Dream Job' worksheet with 5 sentences using 'have to'
Draw a picture of your dream job and label 3 things you have to do
Interview a family member about their job and write 2 sentences using 'have to'
tip: Use Moroccan job examples (like 'tour guide' in Oujda) to make the lesson culturally relevant. Teens respond better when they can connect the language to their local context.
